record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.original_question: For the phonon problem in Euclidean random matrices, how can one compute the very-low-momentum spectral properties correctly by analyzing the two-loop contribution to the self-energy, beyond the one-loop result that gives the asymptotic linewidth scaling?

evidence.quote: The result (119) for the asymptotic regime p << 1 has been found at the one loop level. In order to predict correctly the spectral properties at very low external momentum p, it turns out that one must study the behavior of the two loop contribution, that can be done in details.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Euclidean random matrix model for scalar phonons defined as follows. Let $x_1,\dots,x_N$ be $N$ points drawn independently and uniformly from a box of volume $V=N/\rho$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ at density $\rho$, and let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth, rapidly decaying potential. Define the $N\times N$ random matrix
$$M_{ij}\;=\;\delta_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^{N} f(x_i-x_k)\;-\;f(x_i-x_j),$$
which is the Hessian of a pairwise potential and plays the role of a dynamical (mass) matrix for scalar vibrations. The phonon Green's function is
$$G(p,\omega)\;=\;\Big\langle\Big[\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{i,j} e^{ip\cdot(x_i-x_j)}\big(\omega^2-M+i0^+\big)^{-1}_{ij}\Big]\Big\rangle,$$
and the self-energy $\Sigma(p,\omega)$ is defined by the Dyson decomposition
$$G(p,\omega)^{-1}\;=\;\omega^2-\varepsilon_0(p)-\Sigma(p,\omega),$$
where $\varepsilon_0(p)=\rho\,(\widehat f(0)-\widehat f(p))$ is the bare dispersion. Expand $\Sigma$ in powers of $1/\rho$ (the loop expansion): the one-loop term $\Sigma^{(1)}$ yields, in the regime of small external momentum $p\ll 1$, an asymptotic phonon linewidth (imaginary part of $\Sigma$ on shell) obeying a known power-law scaling in $p$.

Problem. Compute the two-loop contribution $\Sigma^{(2)}(p,\omega)$ to the self-energy of this model in the very-low-momentum regime $p\to 0$, and use it to determine the correct leading behavior of the phonon spectral function (in particular the linewidth and dispersion relation) at very low momentum, going beyond the one-loop asymptotic result.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return specific results on the explicit two-loop self-energy computation for very-low-momentum phonons in the Euclidean random matrix model. General references on Euclidean random matrices and phonon localization exist, but no authoritative source confirming a complete two-loop calculation and the resulting low-p spectral properties was located, so the current status is not determinable from available evidence.
